# Scope & Contracts Checklist: Account Onboarding and Discovery

**Purpose**: Validate requirements-writing quality in four dimensions — P1/P2 tier completeness,
testability of acceptance criteria, out-of-scope leakage, and the cross-spec contracts specs 3, 5,
and 6 inherit from this one
**Created**: 2026-08-23
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

**Scope of this review**: spec 002's *requirements*, not its implementation. Cross-spec items ask
whether this spec specifies a seam well enough for spec 3 (findings/SDA), spec 5 (cost), and
spec 6 (coverage advisor) to build against it.

## P1/P2 Tier Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Is every functional requirement assigned a P1 or P2 tier, or is tiering only applied at the requirement-group heading level? [Completeness, Spec §Requirements]
- [ ] CHK002 Are the lettered requirements added during clarification (FR-003a, FR-009a/b/c, FR-010a, FR-011a, FR-026a) covered by their group's tier, or do they inherit ambiguously? [Gap, Spec §Requirements]
- [ ] CHK003 Does the spec state which success criteria become unverifiable if FR-033 (scan history, P2) is dropped entirely? [Gap, Spec §FR-033]
- [ ] CHK004 Is coverage-as-data's tier reasoning — P1 foundation because P1 enrichment itself depends on it existing, not P2 despite being extensible — stated in the spec rather than left implicit? [Clarity, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK005 Are the P1 requirements self-contained — does any P1 requirement (e.g. FR-019's enrichment) depend on a capability only the P2 FR-020 introduces? [Consistency, Spec §Requirements]

## Acceptance Criteria Testability & Measurability

- [ ] CHK006 Is FR-024's "bounded number of retries" quantified in the requirement itself, rather than only in Assumptions? [Clarity, Spec §FR-024]
- [ ] CHK007 Is FR-025's "MUST be limited" concurrency ceiling quantified anywhere, or is it an unquantified adjective? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-025]
- [ ] CHK008 Can SC-002's ">95% of actual resources... verified by manual sampling" be objectively repeated by two different reviewers and reach the same pass/fail verdict, given the sample size and method are undefined? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK009 Is FR-003a's "sufficient entropy that it cannot be practically guessed" quantified (e.g. a minimum bit length), or left as a qualitative judgement call? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003a]
- [ ] CHK010 Is each of SC-001 through SC-009 independently verifiable without silently depending on another SC's outcome as an unstated precondition? [Consistency, Spec §Success Criteria]
- [ ] CHK011 Does every acceptance scenario across User Stories 1–4 state an observable outcome rather than an internal state change? [Measurability, Spec §User Scenarios]
- [ ] CHK012 Are the "Independent Test" statements on User Stories 3 and 4 genuinely testable with User Story 1 as their only prerequisite, or do they implicitly assume User Story 2's admin surface also exists? [Coverage, Spec §User Scenarios]

## Scope Boundary Integrity — Out-of-Scope Leakage

- [ ] CHK013 Does any requirement imply notifying a resource owner directly, rather than surfacing findings on a dashboard — which both this spec's Out of Scope section and spec 1's MVP cut forbid? [Conflict, Spec §Out of Scope]
- [ ] CHK014 Does any requirement authorize a write, modify, or remediation action against a scanned account, beyond the read-only verification action FR-007 explicitly permits? [Conflict, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK015 Is there a requirement — not merely an absence — establishing that this spec introduces no AI/model-inference code on the discovery or enrichment path, consistent with constitution Principle IV? [Gap, Spec §Requirements]
- [ ] CHK016 Are the Out of Scope entries (tag validation, non-AWS providers, permanent deregistration, the AI coverage advisor) phrased as testable exclusions a reviewer could check a PR against, or are they narrative statements only? [Measurability, Spec §Out of Scope]
- [ ] CHK017 Does the spec bound what a future spec may read from this spec's inventory without a state-changing side effect, or could a downstream spec introduce a write path through the connector interface without violating any requirement written here? [Gap, Spec §FR-014]

## Cross-Spec Contract Consistency

- [ ] CHK018 Does the spec state precisely what guarantee the connector interface (FR-014) makes to spec 6's future coverage advisor, or only that spec 6 "reads coverage configuration as data" without specifying the read path's shape? [Gap, Spec §Dependencies]
- [ ] CHK019 Is the boundary between this spec's `resource` detail payload (FR-013) and spec 3's consumption of that same data specified anywhere, or does spec 3 need to reverse-engineer the shape from this spec's implementation? [Gap, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK020 Does this spec reference SDA grouping or ownership attribution in a way that could conflict with spec 3's delegated authority over those semantics (spec 1 FR-055), given the resource's parent-relationship field this spec already populates? [Consistency, Spec §Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK021 Is it specified whether spec 3's finding-closure logic reads this spec's deleted-resource marker (FR-030) directly, or does this spec leave that integration point for spec 3 to discover on its own? [Gap, Spec §FR-030]
- [ ] CHK022 Does the spec state whether spec 5's cost-ingestion can rely on the resource detail payload's shape being stable across resource types it wasn't originally enriched for, or is that left as an unstated assumption? [Ambiguity, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK023 Is the connector protocol's guarantee to a future non-AWS provider (Out of Scope: "interface only") specified precisely enough that a hypothetical second-provider author would know what to implement, or does FR-014 only assert the boundary exists without describing its shape? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014]

## Edge Case → Requirement Traceability

- [ ] CHK024 Are the performance/scale expectations for a "very large account" (Edge Cases) quantified anywhere, or only described qualitatively as "must not appear stuck"? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK025 Does a requirement cover an admin attempting to reactivate an account that was never deactivated, or only the reverse case? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-009c]

## Ambiguities, Assumptions & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK026 Is the assumption that ARNs are stable identifiers for the life of a resource (FR-015's basis) validated against known AWS exceptions, or asserted without caveat? [Assumption, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK027 Does FR-009 ("refuse duplicate registration") explicitly state that a deactivated account counts as an existing duplicate for this purpose, or is that only inferable from FR-009c's cross-reference? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009, §FR-009c]
- [ ] CHK028 Are the three-role acceptance-matrix cells in SC-009 each traceable to the specific FR that establishes that cell's expected allow/refuse outcome, or does SC-009 assert the matrix without per-cell citation? [Traceability, Spec §SC-009]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- A "no" answer is not automatically a defect. For a spec that hands off to three downstream specs, leaving some integration detail for the owning spec to specify can be the right call — several items above (CHK018, CHK019, CHK021, CHK022) are asking whether the delegation is *stated*, not whether the content is present, matching spec 1's own checklist precedent
